title: Slack for project managers on Mac: lists, canvases and workflows in Slack 4.53
metaTitle: Slack for Project Managers on Mac: Lists, Canvases, Workflows
description: Slack for project managers on Mac: run tasks in Lists, plans in Canvases, and automatic updates with Workflow Builder. Covers plan limits and common mistakes.
targetKeyword: slack for project managers on mac
intro: Slack for project managers on Mac runs on three features: Lists for tasks, Canvases for plans and meeting notes, and Workflow Builder for automatic status updates. All three need a paid Slack plan, so check your plan before you build a process around them. This page shows where each one lives in the Mac app, what it costs, and what to ask Lazur when you get stuck.
tldr: Lists track tasks. On the Mac app, use Home > Files > plus button > List. Pro and Business+ allow 1,000 items and subtasks per list.
Canvases hold the plan and meeting notes. Deleted canvases can be restored only within 24 hours.
Workflow Builder posts updates when a list item changes. Slack's help pages name menus differently, so trust the labels on your screen.
Lists, Canvases and Workflow Builder need a paid plan. Pro starts at $7.25 per user per month billed annually.

blocks.text: Most project managers on Mac use Slack in three layers. A channel holds the conversation. A List holds the tasks. A Canvas holds the plan and the meeting notes. You can run a small project with channels and messages alone. Once several people own pieces of the work, messages get buried and tasks disappear under chat. Lists and Canvases fix that, but only on a paid plan.
Start with a project channel from the starter kit

Slack ships a Project starter kit template. On the Mac app, click the plus button in the sidebar, select Channel, then choose Project starter kit. You get three pieces at once. A project overview canvas holds the description, goals, team and resources. A task tracker list starts with three placeholder tasks. Workflows handle status updates and welcome new members.

Replace the placeholder tasks before your team starts asking where the work lives. Write real task names and fill in the columns your team needs. Delete anything you do not use. Leftover placeholders make the project look unfinished to a client.

Check permissions before you invite anyone. By default, anyone in the channel can edit the canvas and change list items. On an internal project, that is often fine. On a client channel, it can let a client change your task list without warning.

blocks.title: Set edit rights first
blocks.text: Before you post the first message, look at who can edit the canvas and the list. Make that decision once, while the channel is still empty.
Track tasks with Lists on the Mac app

A List works like a table of items, with subtasks under each one. To make a new list on desktop, use Home > Files > plus button > List. To start from a template, use Files > Lists > See all next to Templates, choose one, then click Use template.

Watch the item cap on long projects. Pro and Business+ allow 1,000 items and subtasks per list. Enterprise Grid allows 5,000. When a list reaches its cap, Slack archives the oldest items automatically. A launch with 900 items is close to the limit, so split it into one list per phase early.

Visibility catches people out. On desktop, a new list is visible only to the people or channels you share it with directly. Set general access to Anyone in your organization can view or Anyone in your organization can edit. Mobile cannot set general permissions, so do this step on the Mac.

blocks.title: Frontline roles cannot create lists
blocks.text: Frontline members cannot create lists or canvases. Check each person's role before you plan who builds the tracker.
Plan and take notes in Canvases

A Canvas is a shared document inside Slack. Use one for a kickoff brief, a risk log, a RACI table or meeting notes. To create one on the Mac app, use Home > Files > plus button > Canvas. To attach a canvas to a channel, click the plus sign in the conversation header, then choose Canvas.

Use each tool for what it does well. A canvas suits prose, decisions and short tables. A list suits work you need to sort and track. Keep one home for each fact. If the launch date lives in a canvas, a list and a thread, someone will eventually read the wrong copy.

Restoring a deleted canvas works only within 24 hours. When a canvas becomes a decision record, copy the final version somewhere your team already checks. That habit takes a few minutes each week and saves arguments later.
Automate status updates with Workflow Builder

Workflow Builder runs a set of steps when something happens in Slack. For project work, the trigger you want is When a list item is updated. It starts a workflow when any item in a chosen list changes. Add Field narrows the trigger to changes in one field, such as Status.

Here is a worked example. Pick your task list. Set the trigger to Status. Add a step that posts a short message to the project channel with the task name, the owner and the blocker. Your team sees a blocker when it happens, not at the Friday meeting.

Find the builder on the Mac app. The current help article says to click Agents & tools in the sidebar, then choose Workflows > New > Build Workflow. If Agents & tools is missing, look under More. The templates article still says More > Templates, so Slack's own pages disagree on menu names. Trust the labels on your screen.

blocks.title: Who can build workflows
blocks.text: By default, all Full Members on paid plans can create workflows. Frontline Members are excluded. Test a new workflow on a dummy task before you point it at the real project list.
Why keep the plan inside Slack at all

Slack's own research makes the case for keeping work near the conversation. The State of Work survey covered 17,000 knowledge workers around the world. Over half of respondents said switching between apps makes it harder to get essential work done.

Treat the 68% figure with care. Slack publishes it from its own research, and the page gives no report year. Use it as a reason to test your setup, not as proof that your team will save 30 minutes a day.
Find things fast with jump, search and unread

Press ⌘K to jump to any channel, person or conversation. Start typing the name, use the arrow keys to pick the match, then press Return. This beats scrolling the sidebar when five project channels look alike.

For text, click the search bar at the top of the window. Narrow results with from: and in: to pick one person or one channel. Search is how you find the one message where the client approved the scope.

Read [how to search messages in Slack on Mac](/how-to/search-messages-in-slack) for the full steps. To catch up on what you missed, read [how to jump to the latest unread message in Slack on Mac](/how-to/jump-to-the-latest-unread-message-in-slack).

blocks.text: Keep notifications from burying the plan
Project channels get loud fast. Mute the channels that do not need your reply, and keep only the few that do. A muted channel still holds its messages, so you can open it when you need to.

Read [how to mute a channel in Slack on Mac](/how-to/mute-a-channel-in-slack) and [how to pause notifications in Slack on Mac](/how-to/pause-notifications-in-slack) for the exact menus. If pings stop coming when they should, check [how to fix Slack notifications on Mac](/how-to/fix-missing-notifications-in-slack).

Put decisions in threads and pin the final one. Open [the Threads view](/how-to/open-the-threads-view-in-slack) each morning to see every thread you follow. Use [how to pin a message in Slack on Mac](/how-to/pin-a-message-in-slack) on the message that holds the final decision, so people stop asking.
What Slack costs per person

Lists, Canvases and Workflow Builder are paid-plan features. The table uses prices from Slack's pricing page. Slack bills per user, so count everyone who will edit a list, not only the project managers.

blocks.text: Run the math before you pick a tier. Ten people on Pro, billed annually at $7.25 per user, pay $72.50 a month between them. The same ten people on Business+ pay $150 a month on the annual rate. Pick the plan your team needs, not the top tier by default.
Mistakes project managers make in Slack

items: Keeping the plan in a canvas and the tasks in messages. Pick one home for each fact.
Leaving default edit access on a client channel, so anyone can change list items.
Creating a list and forgetting general access. Teammates see nothing until you share it.
Letting a long project run into the 1,000 item cap, so the oldest items get archived.
Deleting a canvas and waiting. Restoring works only within 24 hours.
Trusting one help page's menu path. Labels change, so read your own sidebar.
Assuming a Frontline teammate can create a list. They cannot.

blocks.text: A worked example: a six-week product launch

Say you run a six-week launch with design, engineering and support. Start from the starter kit, then rename the channel to match the launch. Fill in the overview canvas first. Goals and team names give the rest of the work a frame.

items: Fill in the project overview canvas with the goal, the team and the links you use.
Replace the three placeholder tasks with real launch tasks and an owner for each.
Create a second list for launch-day checks. Use Files > Lists > See all if you want a template.
Add a workflow on the task list. Trigger on Status, then post blockers to the channel.
Open the Threads view each morning, and pin the final decision on every workstream.

blocks.text: Check the list size once a week. A list at 300 items is fine. A list near 1,000 needs splitting, or the oldest items will get archived. Write the split date in the canvas, so the team knows where to look.
How Lazur helps with project work in Slack

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on screen. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut, and it answers out loud.

Lazur points, guides, drafts and dictates. It does not click buttons or operate Slack for you. Ask where a control is, and Lazur circles it and labels it. Ask how to do something, and Lazur walks you one click at a time, waiting for each click.

Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. That helps with status updates, because you can say the update aloud and review the text before you post. You still press send yourself.

Research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs through the Lazur for Chrome extension. It comes back with a summary and a report. Use it for background checks, such as the list limit on your plan, while you keep working in Slack.
Where Slack alone falls short

Slack handles messages, light tracking and documents well. If you need timelines, dependencies or budgets, a dedicated project tool may fit better. This page does not compare those tools, so check their own pricing pages.

faq.question: Can I use Lists and Canvases on the free Slack plan?
faq.answer: Slack's help pages list Lists, Canvases and Workflow Builder as paid-plan features. The free plan also shows 90 days of message history. Check Slack's pricing page for your plan before you build a process around these tools.

faq.question: Does Lazur control Slack for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate other apps. It points at controls, guides you one click at a time, answers questions about your screen, and drafts or dictates text. Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for any app.

faq.question: Why can't my teammate see the list I just made?
faq.answer: On desktop, a list is visible only to people or channels you share it with directly by default. Set general access to Anyone in your organization can view or can edit. Mobile cannot set general permissions, so make that change on the Mac.

faq.question: What happens when a list gets full?
faq.answer: Pro and Business+ allow 1,000 items and subtasks per list. When a list reaches its limit, Slack archives the oldest items automatically. Split long projects into several lists before you reach the cap.

faq.question: Can I restore a deleted canvas?
faq.answer: Only within 24 hours. Slack's canvas help page says deleted canvases can be restored only within that window. After that, plan on rebuilding the content, so copy the final decisions somewhere safe early.

faq.question: Which version of Slack should I use on Mac?
faq.answer: Slack's Mac download page lists version 4.53.280. The page shows no release date and no minimum macOS version. If your menus look different from this page, update the app and check the help article again.

faq.question: Where do I find Workflow Builder on the Mac app?
faq.answer: The current help article says to click Agents & tools in the sidebar, then choose Workflows > New > Build Workflow. If you do not see Agents & tools, look under More. Menu names vary between help articles, so trust the labels on your screen.
